name: Bamali
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Robinson, Rachel (2023) Chopechop (Bamali): A Provisional Analysis of Lexical Tone (SIL); sil.org access blocked (403).

sources.citation: Robinson, Rachel. 2024. Chopechop (Bamali): An introduction to grammatical marking in the verb phrase. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon, draft ms., 31 pp. SIL archive entry 100172.
sources.note: Nothing. TAM, mood, negation, clause linking, with segmental and tonal (floating-tone) morphemes and an appendix on tone orthography; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Robinson, Rachel. 2023. Chopechop (Bamali): A Provisional Analysis of Lexical Tone. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 16 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 98110.
sources.note: Nothing. Whole paper is lexical tone: noun roots fall into four underlying tone groups /H, L, HL, LH/, verb roots into /H, L/; L noun-class prefixes; contour simplification onto echo vowels after glottal stop; floating H after verbs. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur.

sources.citation: Grant, Caroline A. 2007. A Rapid Appraisal Survey of Bamali. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2007-009. 13 pp. (also 1993 Yaoundé version, SIL entry 47444).
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic rapid-appraisal survey (120-item wordlist mentioned, not printed). Notes Wanki 1990 MA thesis as the only prior linguistic study.

sources.citation: Moguo, F. 2008. A Study of Noun Morphology and the Nominal Construction in Chopechop. Mémoire de Maîtrise, University of Yaoundé 1.

sources.note: Yaoundé maîtrise theses on Grassfields languages usually open with a phonology sketch (segments, syllable, tone, sometimes a remark on stress); only other descriptive work on the language.

sources.note: Alphabet/tone-marking primer; low chance of a stress remark but documents the orthographic treatment of prosody.
